Sourdough bread 👍👍👍
Sep 2024 • Solo
Torino Bakery is a fantastic spot for fresh, high-quality baked goods. Their bread is outstanding, with the sourdough being the absolute highlight—crispy on the outside, soft and flavorful on the inside. The grissini is also a nice touch, perfect as a light snack or an accompaniment to meals.

For those with a sweet tooth, the brownies are rich and decadent, while the apple and lemon tarts strike a perfect balance between tartness and sweetness.

However, one downside is the atmosphere. It seems the bakery caters primarily to expats, which can leave local Vietnamese customers feeling less welcomed. It’s something I hope they work on because the quality of their products deserves to be enjoyed by everyone equally.

Overall, the food is exceptional, but the customer experience could use some improvement.

Horrid customer service
Apr 2024 • Couples
As long time residents of Danang, we have ordered from Torino multiple times and eaten in the restaurant a fair few times as well. 
Tonight happened to be one such night that we were dining in. Our order is pretty standard - one pizza and one of their pastas both of which we usually enjoy. We got the homemade tagliatelle tonight and with the first bite we could tell something wasn’t right. It tasted… stale almost. We called the waiter and asked to return the dish and ordered another pasta dish immediately while we continued to enjoy our pizza. 
Instead of just accepting that something may have been wrong and bringing us the new pasta, the waiters came to our table not once, not twice but four times to justify why their pasta was actually good and perhaps we were wrong. “Oh no it is probably the mushroom smell that you didn’t like” “Oh maybe you should taste the bolognese by itself so you know it’s tasting fine” “Oh our chef is afraid you may not like the new pasta as well” 
Good customer service (and we are in the hospitality business ourselves) is simply saying Alright, we’re sorry you didn’t enjoy this, we’ll bring you the other pasta as soon as it’s ready. Instead we felt harassed as we sat there trying to salvage what was left out of this terrible experience. 
We’re not children, this isn’t our first time eating Italian food, or eating at Torino. What in fact bothered us the most was the fact that we saw the chef walking up to about 5 meters away from us to instruct the waiters about what to come and tell us next. It would have been a simple one time visit for him to come to our table if he had so much justifications for this dish being bad. 
Torino has definitely lost a customer in me.
